title: How can you practise case interview thinking in ten minutes a day?
description: A case asks you to remember an objective, interpret information and speak at the same time. The most useful practice looks like those real tasks.
hook: A case asks you to hold a goal in your head, take in new information and talk, all at once. You can practise that, a little each day. Here is how.
body:
Why this matters

A case asks you to remember an objective, interpret information and speak at the same time. The most useful practice looks like those real tasks. Brain-training games can be enjoyable extras, but improving at the game does not guarantee better interview performance.

Three exercises (10 minutes a day)

Mental recap

Listen to two minutes of a business interview, pause, and explain the three most important points in 60 seconds. Keep the message short and organised.

Mental arithmetic

Practise percentages, growth rates, margins, large-number division and break-even maths. Explain your approach before calculating.

Working-memory challenge

Read a short business problem, put it away, then recall the objective, key figures and possible drivers. Do not rely only on a score from a brain-training game.

Keep it small

Short and regular beats long and occasional. Ten minutes most days will do more than two hours on a Sunday. Tick it off and move on with your day.

Try this now

Read this, then look away and recall it: "A gym chain's revenue rose 5% last year, but profit halved. The CEO wants profit restored within 12 months." Say the goal, the two key numbers and two possible causes. If you got all of them, increase the length next time.

Train the actual mental task

Read a short business paragraph once, close it, and write down the objective, two facts and one open question. Then explain in 30 seconds how you would investigate the question. This practises holding a problem in mind while selecting the next step, which resembles the demands of a case more closely than memorising isolated trivia.

A second exercise is to summarise an unfamiliar chart in one sentence after 60 seconds of inspection. Revisit it the next day and check whether you remember the relationship and the decision implication, not just the axes.

Use a simple log of recurring errors. If you repeatedly lose the client's objective after a calculation, put it in a box at the top of your page and point back to it after every result. Transfer to case performance must be tested, not assumed from success in a brain-training app.
outro: All three routines, with links to free tools, are on the interview skills page. Next in this topic: How can you learn to speak more clearly in a case interview?
